scenes.tts: A Schwann cell meets a large axon and wraps it in dozens of turns. Beside a thin axon, it wraps nothing. Who decides?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Axon Sets the Dose. Two Schwann cells: one wrapping a large axon, one holding thin axons in grooves. Question: glia or axon?
scenes.narration: A Schwann cell meets a large axon and wraps it in dozens of turns. Beside a thin axon, it wraps nothing. Who decides?

scenes.tts: In the nineteen seventies, two laboratories swapped Schwann cells between nerves.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Aguayo laboratory; Weinberg and Spencer, 1970s. Schwann cells lift out of one nerve and move into another.
scenes.caption: In the 1970s, two laboratories swapped Schwann cells between nerves.
scenes.narration: In the 1970s, two laboratories swapped Schwann cells between nerves.

scenes.tts: Schwann cells from a nerve with bare axons now meet axons that are normally myelinated. What do they do?
scenes.visual: The moved Schwann cells sit beside large axons in their new nerve. On screen: Predict.
scenes.narration: Schwann cells from a nerve with bare axons now meet axons that are normally myelinated. What do they do?

scenes.tts: They myelinated their new axons. The reverse swap gave the reverse result. In peripheral nerve, the axon decides.
scenes.visual: The moved cells wrap; in the reverse swap, cells sit bare beside thin axons. Bold label: in peripheral nerve, the axon decides.
scenes.narration: They myelinated their new axons. The reverse swap gave the reverse result. In peripheral nerve, the axon decides.

scenes.tts: So the axon must carry a signal. The main one is neuregulin one, type three, a protein on the axon's surface.
scenes.visual: Neuregulin-1 type III drawn as small tethered marks along the axon membrane.
scenes.caption: So the axon must carry a signal. The main one is neuregulin-1 type III, a protein on the axon's surface.
scenes.narration: So the axon must carry a signal. The main one is neuregulin-1 type III, a protein on the axon's surface.

scenes.tts: It stays tethered near the axon membrane, so a Schwann cell reads it mainly by touch.
scenes.visual: A Schwann cell process touches the axon; the tethered marks light where they meet.
scenes.caption: It stays tethered near the axon membrane, so a Schwann cell reads it mainly by touch.
scenes.narration: It stays tethered near the axon membrane, so a Schwann cell reads it mainly by touch.

scenes.tts: Two receptors on the Schwann cell read it, erb bee three and erb bee two. Paired, they signal.
scenes.visual: On the Schwann cell: ErbB3 with a bound neuregulin and a dim kinase; ErbB2 with no ligand and a bright kinase; the two pair and light up.
scenes.caption: Two receptors on the Schwann cell read it, ErbB3 and ErbB2. Paired, they signal.
scenes.narration: Two receptors on the Schwann cell read it, ErbB3 and ErbB2. Paired, they signal.

scenes.tts: A large axon has more membrane per unit length. If the density is similar, it carries more type three. Could the amount be the message?
scenes.visual: A thin and a thick axon side by side, tethered marks at the same spacing on both, so the thick one carries more. Label: if density is similar.
scenes.caption: A large axon has more membrane per unit length. If the density is similar, it carries more type III. Could the amount be the message?
scenes.narration: A large axon has more membrane per unit length. If the density is similar, it carries more type III. Could the amount be the message?

scenes.tts: Give mice half the normal type three. What happens to the sheath, and to the gee ratio?
scenes.visual: Empty genotype table: rows none, half, normal, extra, extra on bare axons. The half row is highlighted.
scenes.caption: Give mice half the normal type III. What happens to the sheath, and to the g ratio?
scenes.narration: Give mice half the normal type III. What happens to the sheath, and to the g ratio?

scenes.tts: The sheaths were thinner for the axon's size, so the gee ratio went up.
scenes.visual: Half row fills: cross-section with a thin sheath; g readout higher. Credit: Michailov, Nave and colleagues, 2004; Taveggia and colleagues, 2005.
scenes.caption: The sheaths were thinner for the axon's size, so the g ratio went up.
scenes.narration: The sheaths were thinner for the axon's size, so the g ratio went up.

scenes.tts: Now let neurons make extra type three. Predict the sheath.
scenes.visual: The extra row is highlighted, its cell empty.
scenes.caption: Now let neurons make extra type III. Predict the sheath.
scenes.narration: Now let neurons make extra type III. Predict the sheath.

scenes.tts: Thicker myelin, and a lower gee ratio. The dose changed in both directions, and the sheath followed both times.
scenes.visual: Extra row fills: thick sheath, lower g readout. Arrows show the dose moved down and up, the sheath following each time.
scenes.caption: Thicker myelin, and a lower g ratio. The dose changed in both directions, and the sheath followed both times.
scenes.narration: Thicker myelin, and a lower g ratio. The dose changed in both directions, and the sheath followed both times.

scenes.tts: Sympathetic axons normally stay bare. Make their neurons produce extra type three, and add Schwann cells. What then?
scenes.visual: Culture dish: sympathetic neurons with bare axons, extra tethered marks added, Schwann cells nearby. The last table row is highlighted.
scenes.caption: Sympathetic axons normally stay bare. Make their neurons produce extra type III, and add Schwann cells. What then?
scenes.narration: Sympathetic axons normally stay bare. Make their neurons produce extra type III, and add Schwann cells. What then?

scenes.tts: The Schwann cells myelinated them.
scenes.visual: The sympathetic axons become wrapped. Credit: Taveggia and colleagues, Salzer laboratory, 2005. The table's last row fills.
scenes.caption: The Schwann cells myelinated them.
scenes.narration: The Schwann cells myelinated them.

scenes.tts: Giving extra signal to axons that would stay bare changed what the glia did. The outcome followed the delivery.
scenes.visual: Side by side: control bare axons; extra type III, wrapped axons. Label: the outcome followed the delivery.
scenes.narration: Giving extra signal to axons that would stay bare changed what the glia did. The outcome followed the delivery.

scenes.tts: That makes type three instructive. It is the same permissive-versus-instructive test as in the neurotrophic hypothesis lesson.
scenes.visual: Label: instructive. A small inset recalls the permissive versus instructive test from the neurotrophic hypothesis lesson.
scenes.caption: That makes type III instructive. It is the same permissive-versus-instructive test as in the neurotrophic hypothesis lesson.
scenes.narration: That makes type III instructive. It is the same permissive-versus-instructive test as in the neurotrophic hypothesis lesson.

scenes.tts: Below a threshold of type three, an axon stays bare. Above it, more type three helps thicken the sheath.
scenes.visual: A dial labelled type III turns up; below a threshold mark the axon is bare, above it a sheath appears and thickens.
scenes.caption: Below a threshold of type III, an axon stays bare. Above it, more type III helps thicken the sheath.
scenes.narration: Below a threshold of type III, an axon stays bare. Above it, more type III helps thicken the sheath.

scenes.tts: If big axons carry more of it, one readout could match the wrap to the axon. That is a proposal, not yet shown.
scenes.visual: Axons of 2, 5 and 10 µm with sheaths that thicken in step. On screen: about 32 turns at 2 µm, 79 at 5 µm, 158 at 10 µm. Small print: illustrative, g = 0.65, about 17 nm per turn.
scenes.narration: If big axons carry more of it, one readout could match the wrap to the axon. That is a proposal, not yet shown.

scenes.tts: The signal is decisive, but not enough alone. The Schwann cell also needs its basal lamina, and its own receptor, G P R one twenty six. Both are required, and not mere on-switches. The basal lamina also tunes the response to neuregulin.
scenes.visual: A thin sheet of extracellular matrix appears around the Schwann cell, labelled basal lamina; a receptor labelled Gpr126 raises cAMP inside. Label: also required; the basal lamina also tunes the response.
scenes.caption: The signal is decisive, but not enough alone. The Schwann cell also needs its basal lamina, and its own receptor, Gpr126. Both are required, and not mere on-switches. The basal lamina also tunes the response to neuregulin.
scenes.narration: The signal is decisive, but not enough alone. The Schwann cell also needs its basal lamina, and its own receptor, Gpr126. Both are required, and not mere on-switches. The basal lamina also tunes the response to neuregulin.

scenes.tts: In nerve, the axon sets the dose, and the dose is the main signal for the wrap.
scenes.visual: Closing card: in nerve, the axon sets the dose, and the dose is the main signal for the wrap.
scenes.narration: In nerve, the axon sets the dose, and the dose is the main signal for the wrap.
